ahidf-has-sanctioned-19751-crore-in.text:
- Claim in post: "The Cabinet extended it in February 2024 — folding in the separate Dairy Infrastructure Development Fund (DIDF) — and raised the outlay to ₹29,610.25 crore through FY2025-26". The post also says: "A loan sanctioned this year can legitimately take several years to fully disburse." It describes the scheme in the present tense ("can borrow up to 90% of project cost").
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The approved window has passed.** The approved scheme period ended 31 March 2026, before this post (10 Aug 2026). The post does not say whether AHIDF is still taking applications.
  - **Disbursement deadline.** One non-official exam-prep summary says applications were accepted until 31 March 2026 and loan disbursements are allowed until 31 March 2027. If correct, the post's 61% undisbursed balance faces a hard deadline. That would undercut "several years to fully disburse".
  - **Outlay wording.** An NDDB addendum (March 2024) gives the revised outlay as ₹29,110.25 crore "up to FY 2025-2026 till 31.03.2026". That matches the post's second figure.
  - **No extension found.** Two searches found no Cabinet decision or Budget 2026-27 line continuing AHIDF beyond 2025-26.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://agridots.com/courses/exam-banking-lateral/finance/financial-schemes/04-02-ahidf
  - https://www.nddb.org/sites/default/files/pdfs/Addendum_dt_26_03_2024.pdf
  - https://visionias.in/current-affairs/news-today/2024-02-02/schemes-in-news/union-cabinet-approves-extension-of-animal-husbandry-infrastructure-development-fund-ahidf-till-2025-26
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. AHIDF's approved period ran to 31 March 2026. We found no Cabinet decision extending it. One secondary source says new applications closed on that date and disbursements must be completed by 31 March 2027. If that is right, much of the undisbursed balance described here has a fixed deadline rather than an open-ended construction lag. We have not confirmed this with the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying."
- Confidence: Low to moderate. The scheme end date (31 Mar 2026) is consistent across sources. The 31 March 2027 disbursement cut-off comes from a single non-official source and is unverified. "No extension" means only that none was found, not that none exists. The department's site and PIB were not reachable.

indias-labour-codes-took-six-years-to.text:

indias-renewable-energy-certificates.text:
- Claim in post: "with a domestic carbon credit market (CCTS) expected to start compliance trading by October 2026". The table says: "Pre-launch for the compliance leg — first trades expected by October 2026". The post also says: "This article read CERC's own draft trading regulation for CCCs directly — No. RA-14026(13)/1/2024-CERC".   - **The trading rules are now final.** CERC notified the final "Terms and Conditions for Purchase and Sale of Carbon Credit Certificates" Regulations, 2026, on 27 Feb 2026 (SolarQuarter, Mercom and law-firm summaries). That was before this post (23 Aug 2026), which cites only the 2024 draft.
  - **Other milestones reported since:**
    - The Indian Carbon Market Portal was launched on 21 Mar 2026.
    - The first compliance date for 2025-26 was 31 Jul 2026.
    - Trading is to run on IEX, PXIL and HPX.
  - **No first issuance or trade was found in any result as of mid-October 2026.**
  - **Timing sources disagree.** A Feb 2025 Carbon Pulse summary quotes BEE as planning to issue credits in October 2026, with trading from November 2026 to January 2027. Some 2026 guides say trading opens "around October 2026".
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://solarquarter.com/2026/03/03/cerc-notifies-2026-regulations-to-formalize-indias-carbon-credit-trading-market/
  - https://mercomindia.com/cerc-issues-rules-to-operationalize-carbon-credit-trading-on-power-exchanges
  - https://carbon-pulse.com/365604/
  - https://icapcarbonaction.com/en/news/compliance-obligations-under-indias-carbon-credit-trading-scheme-enter-force-seven-sectors
  - https://www.saurenergy.com/solar-energy-news/indias-carbon-market-edges-toward-its-first-trade-12482615
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. CERC notified its final Carbon Credit Certificate trading regulations on 27 February 2026, replacing the 2024 draft cited below. As of mid-October 2026 this blog had found no report of a first compliance trade. Earlier statements attributed to BEE pointed to certificates being issued in October 2026 and trading from November, so the 'by October 2026' start may slip."
- Confidence: several summaries agree on the CERC notification date. Whether issuance or trading has started is unverified: no source confirms it either way, and the BEE, IEX and CERC sites were not reachable. The October window has not fully closed, so severity is MEDIUM rather than HIGH. A follow-up check after 31 Oct 2026 is advisable.

  - **2025-26 output beat the target.** The Ministry's Third Advance Estimates for 2025-26 were released 27–28 May 2026, before the post's 24 July 2026 information date. They put foodgrain output at a record 376.563 MT, above the 362.5 MT target.
  - **Crop figures:** rice 154.024 MT, wheat 120.657 MT, maize 55.093 MT.
  - **The 2024-25 base was revised.** These releases put 2024-25 at 357.732 MT, not the 353.96 MT in the post.

The Ministry of Agriculture's Third Advance Estimates for 2025-26 (released late May 2026) put foodgrain output at a record 376.56 MT, above the 362.5 MT target cited below, with wheat at 120.66 MT. The same release revised 2024-25 to 357.73 MT. The demand-floor argument below is unchanged; if anything, it is stronger."

- Claim in post: "One senior industry official cautioned that the comfortable pricing window "may remain comfortable until August 2026, after which China could again start imposing stringent curbs."" The cost model also "identifies a crossover at approximately $10.3/MMBtu delivered gas price, solving (gas price × 30 MMBtu/tonne) + $110/tonne against the cheapest tender of this cycle, $419/t (Nov-25)."

refiners-won-exemption-fight-biofuels.text:
- Claim in post: "EPA's remand decisions on the 2016–2024 exemption petitions after Sinclair and Alon, and how many RINs come back to the market." This is listed under "What to watch". Elsewhere the post says "It also reallocates 70% of the gallons exempted for 2023–25: roughly 0.99 billion RINs in 2026 and 1.04 billion in 2027." The headline card reads "70%Share of 2023–25 exempted gallons EPA reallocated to other refiners".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **EPA has acted on exemptions several times since the cases the post describes. The post (3 Oct 2026) mentions none of these actions.**
    - **22 Aug 2025:** EPA decided 175 petitions from 38 refineries for compliance years 2016–2024. It granted 63 in full and 77 in part (50%), denied 28 and found 7 ineligible. EPA's technical report puts the total exempted at 5,340 million RINs. One summary (ALL4) says EPA ruled on 16 more petitions by 7 Nov 2025.
    - **3 Aug 2026:** EPA decided at least one 2024 petition, which it reissued on 31 Aug.
    - **31 Aug 2026:** EPA decided 34 petitions for the 2025 compliance year: 18 full exemptions, 11 partial, 3 denied, 2 ineligible. That is about 1.76 billion RINs across 29 refineries. EPA also moved the 2025 RVO compliance date by 30 days to 1 Oct 2026.
  - **Reallocation is moving beyond 70%.** EPA said it would propose, before the end of October 2026, reallocating 100% of the difference between projected and actual 2025 exempted volumes into the 2026 and 2027 RVOs. OPIS describes this as a "proposed 100% reallocation into 2026, 2027 RVOs".
  - No result reported a D.C. Circuit ruling on the Set 2 petitions.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://eponline.com/articles/2025/08/22/epa-clears-backlog-of-small-refinery-exemptions.aspx
  - https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2025-08/420r25010.pdf
  - https://www.all4inc.com/4-the-record-articles/u-s-epa-processes-renewable-fuel-standard-small-refinery-exemption-backlog/
  - https://www.epa.gov/renewable-fuel-standard/august-31-2026-decisions-petitions-rfs-small-refinery-exemptions
  - https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/09/epa-issues-decisions-on-small-refinery-exemptions
  - https://www.opis.com/resources/energy-market-news-from-opis/industry-reaction-mixed-on-epas-2025-sre-decisions-with-proposed-100-reallocation-into-2026-2027-rvos/
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. EPA has acted on exemptions beyond the cases described here. In August 2025 it decided 175 petitions for 2016–2024, granting most of them in full or in part. On 31 August 2026 it granted full or partial exemptions to 29 refineries for 2025, about 1.76 billion RINs, and said it would propose reallocating 100% of the 2025 shortfall into the 2026–27 obligations. That would go beyond the 70% reallocation in the Set 2 rule (EPA, as summarised by trade and legal press). The post's central point, that EPA's discretion to reallocate decides RIN prices, still stands and these actions reinforce it."

the-levelised-cost-of-hydrogen.text:
- Claim in post: "The first real, competitively bid supply contracts awarded under SIGHT tell a different current story: $4.21 per kilogram (₹397) for Indian Oil Corporation and $4.11 per kilogram (₹387) for the Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum refineries. That's the actual, market-tested production cost today, not a projection — and it sits at roughly two-and-a-half to three times the Mission's own 2030 target"
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **A lower bid came in before this post was published.** The Numaligarh Refinery (NRL) green hydrogen tender closed in February 2026 at a record low of ₹279/kg, about $3.08/kg, excluding taxes. The winner was NeuEN Green Energy, a BPCL–Sembcorp 50:50 JV, for 10,000 tpa. That is about 2.1× the $1.50 target, not 2.7–2.8×.
  - **The post's ₹397 and ₹387 appear to include 18% GST.**
    - IOCL Panipat: L&T was reported at ₹336/kg excluding GST and ₹397 including GST.
    - HPCL Visakhapatnam: Ocior Energy was reported at ₹328/kg excluding GST. By this reviewer's arithmetic, ₹328 × 1.18 ≈ ₹387.
    - So the post compares a tax-inclusive price with a plant-gate target.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/energy-transition/021226-indias-numaligarh-hydrogen-tender-ends-at-record-low-rupees-279kg
  - https://solarquarter.com/2026/03/24/bpcl-sembcorp-wins-nrl-green-hydrogen-deal-at-record-%e2%82%b9279-kg/
  - https://visionias.in/current-affairs/upsc-daily-news-summary/article/2026-02-17/the-economic-times/science-and-technology/green-hydrogen-tender-records-lowest-ever-bid
  - https://bioenergytimes.com/ocior-energy-wins-bid-to-supply-green-hydrogen-to-hpcls-visakhapatnam-refinery/
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. The $4.11–4.21/kg figures below appear to include 18% GST. Excluding tax, the IOCL and HPCL awards were reported at about ₹336 and ₹328/kg. A later refinery tender, for Numaligarh in February 2026, set a reported record low of ₹279/kg (about $3.08/kg) excluding taxes. That is roughly twice the $1.50/kg target rather than 2.7–2.8 times. The gap is narrower but still large."
- Confidence:
  - Numaligarh ₹279/kg: three summaries agree. One (Vision IAS) did not name the winner.
  - IOCL ₹336 ex-GST: one summary, source not clearly attributed.
  - HPCL ₹328: one source, with an ambiguous date stamp.
  - The GST reading of ₹387 is reviewer inference.
